FLY TYING / BEGINNERS

How to tie a San Juan Worm

One fly, eight clear steps. Gather the materials, follow each stage, and check the finished shape before you start the next one.

Castward field notes Updated 11 November 2026
At a glance
Pattern
San Juan Worm
Lesson
8 illustrated steps
Goal
Secure wraps • clear eye
Start here

Quick answer

Take one stage at a time. Keep the hook eye clear, use only the material the step needs, and check each tie-in before you move on.

On this page

  1. Lay out the materials
  2. Tie it, one step at a time
  3. Your finished fly

01

Lay out the materials

These sizes are a starting recipe. Test the hook and materials together before you tie a batch.[1]

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

PartFor this version
HookSize 12 or 14 nymph hook
ThreadRed 6/0
BodyRed fine Ultra-Chenille
FinishOptional head cement
02

Tie it, one step at a time

  1. 01

    Set the hook

    Clamp the lower hook bend with the shank level.

    Bench tip Keep the point clear of your fingers.

  2. 02

    Lay a thread base

    Cover the shank with red thread. Stop at the bend.

    Bench tip A full base helps the chenille grip.

  3. 03

    Cut the chenille

    Cut a short red chenille length with enough material to extend beyond both ends of the hook.

    Bench tip Trim to your preferred length at the end.

  4. 04

    Anchor the rear

    Bind the chenille on top at the bend, leaving a soft tail behind.

    Bench tip Keep the chenille above the hook.

  5. 05

    Move the thread forward

    Lift the front chenille clear. Wrap the thread to just behind the eye.

    Bench tip Do not trap the lifted chenille.

  6. 06

    Anchor the front

    Lower the chenille onto the shank. Secure it behind the eye with a short thread band.

    Bench tip Leave the front tip free.

  7. 07

    Tie the finish

    Whip finish on the front band. Snip the thread.

    Bench tip Do not cut the chenille.

  8. 08

    Trim and inspect

    Trim the two ends with scissors. Check the eye and tug each end gently.

    Bench tip This beginner version uses cut ends; no flame is needed.

[1]
03

Your finished fly

  • ✓The hook eye stays clear.
  • ✓The materials stay put under a gentle tug.
  • ✓The point and hook gap remain usable.
04

Small mistakes, simple fixes

Swipe the table to compare all columns.

What you seeTry this
Chenille under the hookKeep it on top at both tie-in points.
Loose endsUse firm thread bands without cutting the core.
A blocked eyeLeave room for the front band.
A few good questions

Before you head out

Can I change the color?

Yes. Keep the same sequence and use comparable materials. Change one feature at a time so you can see its effect.

What if the fly looks uneven?

Check the secure wraps and open eye first. Keep this fly as a reference, then repeat the recipe with less material.
